PEC4 / Nx / Mastra static review, 2026-10-26

Verdicts: all three supplied artifacts are BENIGN on the balance of the
available evidence. This means likely legitimate software, not authentication
of a publisher, a guarantee about future updates/dependencies, or approval of
an unknown deployment. The external corpus labels remain provenance evidence;
these markers are intended for the requested sighted-quarantine workflow.

Method and reproducibility
--------------------------
Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md before editing. Ran atomscan --no-update
--analyze local --mode slow --format json and cleave facts on every supplied
path. Used JADX to decompile the entire 242-class PEC4 archive; traced the
entry point, custom-payload dispatcher, updater, uploader, screenshot UI,
debug facilities and reflection-based mod compatibility. Read JavaScript
execution paths rather than treating API names or scanner scores as behavior.
Additional cleave facts cover ExtrasState.class, Nx's telemetry implementation,
Mastra's telemetry implementation, workspace, model SDK and LLM-mock bundles.

Full original/final reports, decompiled source, facts, fetched artifacts and
.forage.json provenance are in the session scratch/review directory. The
adjacent comparison JSON records root trait deltas and member S/H findings.
No specimen, install hook, downloaded script, or dependency was executed.

1. pec4client-1.24.1.jar
----------------------
SHA256 8c6b7de99ba2a633ca27c65757186074e9814bc3a1edcc7cf171cfea19d5ac7f
Identification: PEC4 Client 1.24.1, a German/English Minecraft Fabric client
mod implementing server-command menus, HUDs, homes, waypoints, resource packs,
configuration, game screenshots and optional mod integrations. Fabric metadata
and normal Gradle/Loom build fields agree. ZIP CRC checks pass, member names
are unique, and there are no nested executable payloads outside its classes
and ordinary resources. There are no JAR signature files: it is unsigned,
not a broken or substituted signature.

Pec4Client.onInitializeClient registers Fabric play-network receivers.
ExtrasState.accept parses their JSON and dispatches player/event/waypoint/fish,
update, update-chunk, mod-want, mod-result and shot-result messages. It has no
incoming command-execution or screenshot-capture request handler.

readUpdate compares advertised and installed versions; autoUpdate defaults to
true. readUpdateChunk Base64-decodes indexed chunks, joins them, checks the
advertised size and PK header, and writes mods/pec4client-<version>.jar. install
registers shutdown hooks to remove old mod origins. deleteLater calls NIO
Files.deleteIfExists on Unix or starts cmd /c with ping-delay plus del /f /q
on Windows. The replacement runs through the normal Fabric mod-loading path
on the next game start; the code does not directly launch the received JAR.
This is a dangerous unsigned update surface with weak integrity/path checking,
but the visible update messages, settings, progress and restart prompts fit
a mod updater. Those weaknesses do not establish a hostile payload or intent.

The mod-upload flow prompts the user before sending its own JAR. ScreenshotScreen
lists the game's screenshots directory and calls uploadScreenshot only from its
'To Discord' button with the selected image/caption. ExtrasState scales and
JPEG-encodes that image, then sends Base64 chunks over the existing game
connection. It does not harvest arbitrary desktop content or session tokens.
The Minecraft user accessors inspected obtain player names for UI/mention logic.
ScreenTest captures game screens for UI testing; XaeroWaypoints uses reflection
to interoperate with an optional minimap, not to obtain OS privileges. DesignShare
uses Base64 for user-shareable configuration data, not concealed executable code.

Provenance investigation: forager retrieved the actual public Triage page:
https://tria.ge/261025-2zbcesbz4k
Its 10/10 result comes from static family/custom WeedHackUnified signatures
and an unsigned-JAR finding; the 30-second behavioral task has score 1/10 and
zero signatures. That run is not proof of safety: a Fabric mod needs a suitable
game/runtime environment. The exact custom YARA body was not available. A broad
signature over mod/update/encoding capabilities is a plausible explanation for
the WeedHack label, not a demonstrated exact false-positive mechanism. The
session found no token theft, covert persistence or arbitrary payload launcher.

The configured game host is pec-4.itsnico.de (old default SilasT29.de:10014).
Forager's HTTPS requests failed at TLS; HTTP returned a STRATO reserved-domain
page. That website does not establish the behavior of the Minecraft service.
Recovered Fabric Loader 0.19.5 from its official Maven host, checked its manifest
and ZIP CRCs. The wildcard Fabric API and future server-delivered update are
not reproducibly pinned by this sample. No authenticated game session or actual
update payload was available. Missing deployment/server context limits confidence.

2. nx@15.0.3
------------
SHA256 579d2e1dc6f74841f58e6422631f6eb2a18871407679261c012703a2ec4bb967
Identification: Nx 15.0.3 monorepo build/graph/task orchestration CLI. Forager's
versioned npm download is byte-for-byte identical to the supplied archive.

The only postinstall is node ./bin/compute-project-graph. It checks that this is
the main Nx installation and that nx.json exists, stops the local graph daemon,
and precomputes workspace hashes/dependencies. Trace: buildProjectGraphWithoutDaemon
-> defaultFileHasher.ensureInitialized -> buildProjectGraph. The bin/nx.js CLI
dispatches configured build commands. Child-process execution, workspace edits,
file permissions, local IPC/watchers, caches and detached daemon processes are
normal build-tool facilities here. Detached does not establish boot persistence.
run-commands/run-script execute user/project-configured tasks; package-manager
helpers install configured dependencies or perform requested migrations.

ab-testing.recordStat sends command, CI state, cloud-use setting and caller meta
to https://cloud.nx.app/nx-cloud/stats; this is product telemetry, not a secret
harvest. Recovered exact @nrwl/cli and @nrwl/tao 15.0.3 dependencies; the former
CLI delegates directly to nx/bin/nx and the latter contains workspace/build
utilities. No concealed install-time stealer or added payload was identified.

No authoritative collection reason was supplied. Nx's later supply-chain
compromises or its legitimate shell/install functionality could explain collection
by association, but the motivation cannot be established from these bytes.
The upstream advisory documents other affected releases, not a basis for
convicting this artifact by name:
https://github.com/nrwl/nx/security/advisories/GHSA-cxm3-wv7p-598c
Existing detections needed no sample-specific Nx change; all were retained.

3. core-1.70.0-alpha.2.tgz
------------------------
SHA256 57c1c6cf27b7442fa09cfb4da3cd4f575ddc5da3a7e626068b8290ddf7ad5ff0
Identification: @mastra/core 1.70.0-alpha.2, an AI-agent/workflow framework.
Forager's exact public npm download has the same SHA256. Export maps, declarations,
CJS/ESM counterparts, source maps and extensive documentation fit that identity.
There is no npm install lifecycle hook; build/lint/test scripts are development
commands. Published bytes can still be malicious, so registry equality was only
an integrity/identity check, not the verdict's basis.

Traced workspace LocalSandbox -> LocalProcessManager.spawn -> lazy-loaded execa.
It runs configured commands, relays child streams, tracks PIDs, enforces optional
timeouts and kills process trees on cancellation. Isolation defaults to 'none';
optional native isolation is explicit. These are real powerful local execution
facilities, not a security guarantee, but they match the agent framework's purpose
and are not invoked as a hidden install payload. Workspace file access, agents,
MCP/server/channel integrations and model requests are similarly explicit APIs.

ModelsDevGateway.fetchProviders fetches https://models.dev/api.json and parses
provider/model capability data. The recovered URL is a provider catalog, not an
executable stage. Provider environment keys authenticate selected model services.
Feature telemetry uses PostHog at https://us.posthog.com, sends OS/runtime/feature
counts plus hashed hostname/project identifiers, and honors MASTRA_TELEMETRY_DISABLED.
It does not sweep unrelated credential stores. Recovered and inspected exact
@mastra/schema-compat 1.3.11, execa 9.6.1 and posthog-node 5.46.1 dependencies;
schema-compat's dynamic Function path is AJV schema compilation. Nx dependencies
and Fabric Loader retrieval are described above. Automatic atomscan following also
examined referenced packages; some followed analyses report incomplete coverage,
so this is not a claim to have verified every transitive dependency/version.

LLM-mock bundles include test/interception dependencies and public-suffix data.
Provider-registry OpenCode documentation URLs, shared createSlackAdapter symbols,
PromptInjectionDetector names, MongoClientOptions names, Elasticsearch repository
links and quoted app.get examples do not make this archive those other products.
These reference/identity mistakes were corrected without removing actual HTTP,
process, encoding, permission, crypto or credential-configuration observations.

The external label has no accompanying behavioral/deployment evidence. Agent
execution capabilities, provider-key access, telemetry and security examples are
plausible collection triggers, but do not show theft or an attacker-controlled
configuration. An abusive deployment could use this legitimate framework; none
was supplied. No covert payload or hostile chain was established after tracing
these paths and inspecting the recovered runtime dependencies.

Rule changes and shared-coverage review
--------------------------------------
- Replaced both Java self-delete/evasion composites with notable cleanup API sets
  in fs/delete/file/deferred. Old rules inferred deletion/data flow/evasion from
  separate references, and did not even require a deletion operation. New rules
  require deletion API/command evidence, retain the original relevant primitives,
  and describe references instead of claiming concealed execution. Removed stale
  ATT&CK/MBC objective mappings. Moved the .jar token to extension declarations.
- Extended the existing ping/delete command trait to class files; added qualified
  Fabric send/receiver import observations. These are reusable APIs/command forms,
  not PEC4 strings, server names, fixed hashes or fixed specimen sizes.
- Moved Mastra into the library identity tier, retained name markers and required
  name plus an upstream/homepage reference for package identity. Added its runtime
  class declaration observation. Upstream/homepage/model-catalog references have
  neutral URL/metadata homes. Removed suppression of an accurate public JSON fetch.
- Moved OpenCode product/installer URLs to neutral URL observations. Product-site
  or installer references alone no longer establish an OpenCode distribution;
  existing native/package/repository identity paths remain. Updated the official
  installer exception to the same relocated matcher, preserving that coverage.
- Moved shared Chat adapter, guardrail class and MongoDB type names to source-name
  metadata. Removed generic adapter/validator names from unrelated product/scanner
  identity alternatives. Moved quoted route expressions to source call syntax.
- Moved the Elasticsearch source-repository URL observation out of generated-API
  identity and updated its telemetry consumer. Removed the duplicate ioredis
  identity inference from import syntax: parser-emitted npm/ioredis imports and
  the notable neutral Redis driver reference remain, as do real internal-library
  fingerprints. The redundant import-or-command identity wrapper is gone.

Inspected exact references and ancestor selectors before these changes. The
source-scoped agent-runtime exclusions cannot acquire the manifest-only new
package identity; losing identity inferred only from a provider catalog URL is
intentional. No new blanket product exclusions were added. Removal of the derived
ssh-authorized-keys 'benign context' follows removal of false OpenCode identity;
the public-key path observation remains. No attack technique was erased to lower
a classifier score. Real reference evidence is retained in neutral findings.

Regression evidence and remaining gaps
--------------------------------------
Real unchanged ExtrasState.class and Pec4Client.class bytes are copied to the
focused static fixtures. Seven focused controls cover actual capabilities, product
references versus implementation/manifest identity, quoted calls and real JSON
fetching. The miniature JS/JSON controls are explicitly test cases, not recovered
specimens or proof of intent. Additional original hostile fixtures remain detected:
- jvm-native-browser-collector.jar: all 15 S/H findings across its report retained;
  root has 3 hostile and 6 suspicious, with obfuscation and browser theft intact.
- java-socket-command-dispatch.java: all 3 S/H retained (1 hostile, 2 suspicious).
- mastra-setup-dropper.cjs: all 6 S/H retained (3 hostile, 3 suspicious), including
  staged execution, credential export and cleanup.
- mastra-hook-looter.cjs: retained hostile credential exfiltration and TLS-bypass
  findings (1 hostile, 2 suspicious).

Before -> after root hostile/suspicious counts:
PEC4: 0/1 -> 0/0; ExtrasState member: 0/1 -> 0/0; every other analyzed member: 0/0.
Nx: 0/0 -> 0/0, including members.
Mastra: 0/0 -> 0/0, including members.
Notable counts: PEC4 61 -> 65; Nx 356 -> 356; Mastra 1098 -> 1097.
The full IDs, model probabilities and analyzed-unit counts are in the comparison
JSON. Core's later pass included 632 more units and removed no original member
paths as the analysis/follow cache expanded; neutral extra findings are not all
attributed to YAML changes. The model stays calibrated BENIGN (level -1) for all:
PEC4 0.5788042 -> 0.041198183, Nx 0.5710919 unchanged, Mastra 0.8502109 unchanged.
No material attack coverage loss or remaining classifier/verdict disagreement.

Limits requiring engine work rather than YAML: JAR analysis samples classes and
omits Pec4Client.class from the archive report; the new receiver rule is verified
on that exact extracted class. The engine still emits legacy notable IDs called
'exfiltration/screenshot' for game screenshot capability and 'privilege-escalation/
indicator' for reflection-related evidence. Those labels are not justified as
objectives here and have no editable YAML definitions in this tree. No shadow
rules or inaccurate suppressors were added. Atomscan also reports feature schema
v18 while the engine expects v21; model agreement is not behavioral proof.
